raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

With several API server processes, `--max-num-queued-tokens` is checked against each process's own prefill backlog, so N API servers admit up to N times the cap. This shares the token count across API servers the way #54746 shares the request count.

Fixes #65265

## Claims

- With `--api-server-count` above 1, `--max-num-queued-tokens` rejects once the prefill backlog summed over all API servers reaches the cap, as the `SchedulerConfig` docs describe.
- The shared counters are allocated when either cap is set, not only with `--max-num-queued-reqs`.
- With one API server nothing changes.

## Validation

New tests, CPU only, which CI runs in the V1 Engine step (`pytest v1/engine`) and the Entrypoints Unit step (`pytest entrypoints/launchers`):

- `test_admission_control.py::test_shared_token_cap_counts_every_api_server`: two `AsyncLLM` API servers, each with a real `OutputProcessor`, share one counter array. 150 + 150 prefill tokens under a cap of 400 are admitted on both; one more 150-token request and both reject.
- `test_admission_control.py::test_shared_token_count_follows_prefill_exit_and_abort`: the shared count drops when a request gets its first token and when a request still in prefill is aborted; the request count is left alone.
- `test_api_server_process_manager.py::test_api_server_processes_share_queued_tokens`: three spawned API server processes share the token count when only `max_num_queued_tokens` is set.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py
```

On main (source files as on main, new tests kept):

```text
E       assert [True, True] == [False, False]
E       AttributeError: 'SharedAdmissionStats' object has no attribute 'get_num_queued_tokens'
KeyError: 'mp_admission_counters'   (in each spawned API server; the test then sees a non-zero exitcode)
FAILED tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py::test_shared_token_cap_counts_every_api_server
FAILED tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py::test_shared_token_count_follows_prefill_exit_and_abort
FAILED tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py::test_api_server_child_adopts_inherited_zmq_listeners[ipc]
FAILED tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py::test_api_server_processes_share_queued_tokens
FAILED tests/entrypoints/launchers/api_server/test_api_server_process_manager.py::test_rust_frontend_spawn_failure_cleans_up_listeners
5 failed, 61 passed
```

With this PR: 2 failed, 64 passed. `tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py`: 26 passed, 34 errors, the same on main and with this PR.

CPU only: macOS 26.6.2 arm64, Python 3.12.1, torch 2.13.0, main `9cd2e98b59`.

Not run yet: `vllm serve` end to end with `--api-server-count 2` (no GPU here). This PR stays a draft until that result is in this description.

## Details

- Each process already owns a 64-byte slot of 8 counters in `SharedAdmissionStats`, and the request count is counter 0. The prefill token total goes into counter 1, and `get_num_queued_tokens()` sums it over all slots, as `get_num_requests()` does.
- `OutputProcessor` writes the total when it can change: after `add_request` (including a streaming-input update), after `abort_requests`, and once at the end of `process_outputs` if a request left prefill, was rejected on arrival or got a new streaming input chunk. Nothing is written unless the counters are shared.
- `check_admission` reads the shared total when the counters exist, like the request cap.
- `APIServerProcessManager` allocates the counters when either cap is set.
- `docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md` and the `check_admission` docstring say both counts are shared across API servers and approximate.

Trade-offs:

- Like #54746's request count, the shared counts are read without a lock: requests that reach different API servers at the same moment can each be admitted, so a burst can pass the cap by up to one request per API server. The docs now say so.
- The written value is `get_num_queued_tokens()`, the walk over this process's requests that `check_admission` already does for each new request when the token cap is set. It runs once per add, abort or output batch, not once per finished request (on one 2.8 GHz Xeon core the walk takes 9 µs with 256 requests in flight, 68 µs with 1,024 and 346 µs with 4,096, half of them in prefill). A running total would be O(1), but every state change, streaming-input updates included, would have to keep it right, and #59097 also changes `get_num_queued_tokens`. I kept the walk and can switch if you prefer.
- With only `--max-num-queued-reqs` set the counters exist, so the token total is still written. If that matters, `AsyncLLM` can tell `OutputProcessor` whether the token cap is set.
- The count is still the full `prompt_len` of each request in prefill. Counting only the prefill work left, the other part #49445 deferred, is a separate change (discussed on #59097). Scheduler stats reach only one API server per step ([scheduler.py#L2662](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/0e5b2ba118cfb3763a3640942e02dd8d93e8ed6c/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2662)), so a scheduler-side count would also need sharing between API servers, and these counters could carry it.

No open issue or PR shares the token cap across API servers (searched `max_num_queued_tokens` and `SharedAdmissionStats`).

AI-assisted; reviewed and tested by me.

@@ -26,7 +26,7 @@ vLLM supports "self-contained" data parallel deployments that expose a single AP
 
 It can be configured by simply including e.g. `--data-parallel-size=4` in the vllm serve command line arguments. This will require 4 GPUs. It can be combined with tensor parallel, for example `--data-parallel-size=4 --tensor-parallel-size=2`, which would require 8 GPUs. When sizing DP deployments, remember that `--max-num-seqs` applies per DP rank.
 
-By contrast, the admission control limits `--max-num-queued-reqs` and `--max-num-queued-tokens` apply to the whole server, not per DP rank: each API server process counts in-flight requests and prefill backlog across all DP ranks it routes to. For example, with `--data-parallel-size=4 --max-num-seqs=256 --max-num-queued-reqs=256`, the deployment rejects new requests once 256 are in-flight in total, even though ranks could jointly run 1024. To keep ranks saturating, size the cap as roughly `data-parallel-size * max-num-seqs` plus the desired queue depth.
+By contrast, the admission control limits `--max-num-queued-reqs` and `--max-num-queued-tokens` apply to the whole server, not per DP rank: each API server process counts in-flight requests and prefill backlog across all DP ranks it routes to. For example, with `--data-parallel-size=4 --max-num-seqs=256 --max-num-queued-reqs=256`, the deployment rejects new requests once 256 are in-flight in total, even though ranks could jointly run 1024. To keep ranks saturating, size the cap as roughly `data-parallel-size * max-num-seqs` plus the desired queue depth. With `--api-server-count` above 1, the API server processes share both counts; requests that reach different API servers at the same moment can each be admitted, so a burst can pass a limit by up to one request per API server.
 
 Running a single data parallel deployment across multiple nodes requires a different `vllm serve` to be run on each node, specifying which DP ranks should run on that node. In this case, there will still be a single HTTP entrypoint - the API server(s) will run only on one node, but it doesn't necessarily need to be co-located with the DP ranks.
